S01.evidence: suggesting that the medication may have exac-erbated his erectile issues
S01.why: Single new patient on semaglutide with worsened ED that improved after stopping it.

S02.evidence: suggested a possible drug-associated neuro-ophthalmic adverse effect
S02.why: New patient with visual disturbance after semaglutide, authors suspect the drug.

S03.evidence: experienced transient intestinal ischemia following his first Wegovy dosage
S03.why: New patient with intestinal ischemia attributed to semaglutide.

S04.evidence: suggesting that metformin was the most likely causative agent
S04.why: New patient with erythema multiforme assessed as probably caused by metformin.

S05.evidence: The Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score was 6 (“probable”)
S05.why: New patient with postmenopausal bleeding judged probably due to semaglutide.

S06.evidence: semaglutide-induced gastroparesis and slow intestinal transit may have contributed to bezoar formation
S06.why: New patient with bezoar obstruction that authors link to semaglutide.

S07.evidence: developed SPM shortly after the self-administered use of semaglutide
S07.why: New patient with pneumomediastinum after semaglutide-related vomiting, presented as a drug consequence.

S08.evidence: suggests a possible association between oral semaglutide and venous thrombosis
S08.why: New adolescent patient with DVT linked as possible to oral semaglutide.

S09.evidence: a rare case of metformin toxicity resulting in biventricular failure
S09.why: New patient with cardiogenic shock attributed to metformin toxicity.

S10.evidence: we present a case of 65-year-old women
S10.why: New patient with metformin-associated lactic acidosis.

S11.evidence: severe acidemia due to MILA precipitated by post-obstructive acute kidney injury
S11.why: New patient with metformin-induced lactic acidosis.

S12.evidence: three patients who developed acute, painless vision loss shortly after initiating semaglutide therapy
S12.why: Own three-patient series with NAION suspected due to semaglutide.

S13.evidence: intentionally ingested 34 g of her prescribed metformin
S13.why: New patient with fatal MALA from metformin overdose, harm attributed to metformin.

S14.evidence: We describe a fatal case of MALA following intentional metformin overdose
S14.why: New patient with fatal MALA caused by metformin overdose.

S15.evidence: severe AKI while on metformin therapy
S15.why: New patient with metformin-associated lactic acidosis.

S16.evidence: confirmed the diagnosis of metformin-associated encephalopathy
S16.why: New patient with encephalopathy attributed to metformin.

S17.evidence: Both patients developed similar cutaneous manifestations during therapy
S17.why: Two new patients with acneiform eruptions temporally associated with semaglutide.

S18.evidence: myopathy probably caused by concomitant use of atorvastatin and almonertinib
S18.why: New patient with myopathy from atorvastatin as interacting suspect drug.

S19.evidence: discontinued several months after starting semaglutide due to acute gallstone pancreatitis
S19.why: New patient on semaglutide with gallstone pancreatitis presented as a potential adverse event.

S20.evidence: temporally related to semaglutide exposure and re-exposure
S20.why: New patient with transient hip osteoporosis possibly linked to semaglutide with rechallenge.
